meta.name: NIT DGP Chatbot — Held-out Evaluation Set
meta.purpose: Measure the RAG pipeline WITHOUT rewarding memorisation. None of these reuse the FAQ knowledge-base wording that was ingested. Applied cases force retrieval + reasoning; out-of-scope cases test honest refusal.

buckets.applied: Scenario/numeric questions. The answer is not a stored string; the model must map a value to a rule. Curation cannot echo its way to a correct answer.
buckets.paraphrased: In-scope rules asked in different words from the FAQ.
buckets.out_of_scope: Facts the regulations do NOT contain. A correct response REFUSES / says it's not in the regulations. Uncheatable by curation — there is nothing to curate.
buckets.partial: The rule exists but a specific number/detail is absent from the PDF. Correct = state the rule, do NOT invent the missing value.
buckets.multi_turn: Second turn uses a pronoun/ellipsis. Tests the contextualize-question step in app.py.

grading.method: Do NOT use exact string match — that rewards echoing. Check each string in expected_facts is present in meaning (a number, grade letter, or yes/no), and that nothing in must_not appears.
grading.score_two_axes_separately: Retrieval: did the right chunk appear in the retrieved context (inspect retriever output)? Answer: given that context, is the final answer correct and faithful? Curation fixes retrieval; you still verify answer.
grading.report: Run this same set against (a) the baseline pipeline and (b) the improved pipeline. Report the before/after delta per bucket — that delta is the evaluation.

turns: I scored 72 in a theory subject. What letter grade is that and how many grade points?
cases.grading_note: 72 is in the 70-79 band -> B -> 8 points. Requires mapping a mark to a band, not echoing the table.

turns: If I get 47 marks in a theory paper, do I pass, and what grade?
cases.grading_note: 35-49 -> P (pass) -> 5 points. Cutoff for F is below 35.

turns: I got 33 in a theory exam. What happens to my grade?
cases.grading_note: Below 35 in theory -> F -> 0 points.

turns: My attendance in a theory course is 55%. Is there any penalty?
cases.grading_note: Below 75% but not below 50% -> reduction of one grade.

turns: What if my attendance drops to 40% in that course?
cases.grading_note: Below 50% but not below 25% -> reduction of two grades.

turns: I only attended 20% of a theory course. Can I still sit the end-semester exam?
cases.grading_note: Below 25% -> debarred from end-sem; must re-register as a regular/backlog course next corresponding semester with one grade reduced.

turns: My final CGPA is 6.8. What class of degree do I get?
cases.grading_note: CGPA >= 6.50 but < 8.00 -> First Class (not Distinction, which needs >= 8.00 with all cleared in regular exams).

turns: I finished with CGPA 8.2, cleared every course in the regular exams, no disciplinary action. What class?
cases.grading_note: CGPA >= 8.00 with all courses cleared in regular exams and no disciplinary conviction -> First Class with Distinction.

turns: My CGPA is 8.0. What percentage is that?
cases.grading_note: % = (CGPA - 0.5) x 10 = (8.0 - 0.5) x 10 = 75%. Must apply the formula, not guess.

turns: I failed a theory paper, then reappeared in the supplementary exam and my marks there would normally be an A. What grade actually goes on my card?
cases.grading_note: Supplementary grade is dropped one letter but not below P: A -> B.

turns: I'm General category, cleared everything first attempt, SGPA 9.1 in semester 1 and 8.9 in semester 2. Am I eligible for a branch change?
cases.grading_note: General/OBC/EWS need SGPA >= 9.00 in BOTH sem 1 and sem 2. Sem 2 = 8.9 < 9.00 -> not eligible. Edge case; a memorised 'branch change needs high SGPA' answer will get this wrong.

turns: I'm SC category with SGPA 8.6 and 8.7 in the first two semesters, all first attempt. Can I apply for a branch change?
cases.grading_note: SC/ST need SGPA >= 8.50 in both semesters. 8.6 and 8.7 both qualify -> eligible.

turns: I failed one laboratory course this semester. Do I have to repeat the whole year?
cases.grading_note: Failing ONE sessional/lab course -> promoted, re-register that course as backlog sessional with the next batch.

turns: What if I fail two lab courses in the same semester?
cases.grading_note: Failing MORE THAN ONE sessional/lab -> repeat the semester by taking re-admission with the next batch.

turns: It's my fourth semester. How many backlog papers can I take alongside my regular courses?
cases.grading_note: From 3rd semester onward: all regular courses + a maximum of 2 backlog courses.

turns: I'm in the 7th year of my 4-year B.Tech and still haven't finished. Can I still be awarded the degree?
cases.grading_note: Max is 6 years for a 4-year programme; one more year only with special Senate approval. 7th year is beyond the normal limit.

turns: For a course that has both theory and a lab component, like a 3-0-2, how much do the end-term and the lab count for?
cases.grading_note: Combined theory+sessional: CA 10%, Mid 20%, End-term 40%, Lab 30%. NOT the theory-only 15/25/60 split.

turns: I was hospitalised and missed my end-semester exam. What are my options?
cases.grading_note: Normally: declared failed -> supplementary with one-grade penalty. With a documented compelling reason: appeal to Dean (Academic) via HOD; a subcommittee may condone the absence and allow the supplementary with FULL credit. 'I' grade until then.

turns: Can I retake a subject I already passed just to improve my grade?
cases.grading_note: Supplementary/backlog exams are only for F or X (absent). No provision to re-sit a passed course for a better grade.

turns: What's the lowest CGPA I can have and still actually graduate?
cases.grading_note: CGPA of 5.00 or higher, minimum grade P in every course, all dues cleared.

turns: Once the registration window closes, can I still swap one of my subjects?
cases.grading_note: Once registered, no changes in the course list are permitted.

turns: My grade card shows 'I' next to a course. What does that mean?
cases.grading_note: I = Incomplete assessment. (X = Absent, RA = Reported Against, W = Withheld — distractors.)

turns: Roughly when does the autumn semester begin?
cases.grading_note: Odd/Autumn semesters commence from the 3rd week of July.

turns: How do I apply for my official transcript, and what's the fee for it?
cases.grading_note: The regulations don't describe the transcript application procedure or fee. Correct = say it's not in the regulations / direct to the Academic Section. FAIL if it invents a procedure or amount.

turns: What's the current semester tuition fee amount?
cases.grading_note: Regulations say fees are 'as prescribed by the Institute' but give no amount. Correct = state the rule, refuse to give a number. FAIL if a rupee figure appears.

turns: What are the exact dates for this year's mid-semester exams?
cases.grading_note: Specific dates live in the Academic Calendar notification, not these regulations. Correct = point to the Academic Calendar. FAIL if it fabricates dates.

turns: Who is the current Head of the Electrical Engineering department?
cases.grading_note: No individual names in the regulations. FAIL if it invents a name.

turns: Exactly how many total credits do I need to graduate with a B.Tech?
cases.grading_note: The regulations state the total credit requirement is the same for all branches and is fixed by the Senate, but give NO number. Correct = explain the rule and say the specific figure isn't in this document. FAIL if it invents a credit count. This is the key faithfulness probe.

turns: What SGPA do I need in the first two semesters to change branch as a General category student?
And for SC/ST students?
cases.grading_note: Turn 1 answer: >= 9.00 in both semesters. Turn 2 must resolve 'for SC/ST students?' to the branch-change SGPA and return >= 8.50 in both. Tests the contextualize-question step.

turns: I failed a theory paper. How do I clear it?
Will there be any penalty on my grade?
cases.grading_note: Turn 1: supplementary exam. Turn 2 'any penalty?' must resolve to the supplementary grade and return one-letter-lower, not below P. Tests pronoun/context carry-over.

turns: For a normal theory course, how are the marks split across the components?
What about a course that also has a lab?
cases.grading_note: Turn 1: CA 15%, Mid 25%, End 60%. Turn 2 must switch to the combined split: CA 10%, Mid 20%, End 40%, Lab 30%. Tests whether follow-up retrieves the right variant.
